contentBlocks.text: Find answers to the most common questions about the SASSA grant appeal process. If you do not see your question here, refer to our detailed appeal guides.

faqs.question: How long do I have to appeal a SASSA decline?
faqs.answer: You have 90 days from the date of your decline notification to file an appeal. Appeals submitted after 90 days will not be accepted.

faqs.question: How long does the appeal process take?
faqs.answer: The tribunal takes 60 to 90 days to issue a ruling. Complex cases may take up to 120 days.

faqs.question: Do I need a lawyer to appeal?
faqs.answer: No. SASSA appeals are designed for self-representation. The online portal guides you through the process.

faqs.question: Can I appeal more than once?
faqs.answer: You cannot appeal the tribunal's decision. However, you can submit a new grant application if your circumstances change.

faqs.question: Do I get paid while my appeal is pending?
faqs.answer: No. Payments only resume if and when your appeal is approved. Backpay is then issued to the original decline date.

faqs.question: How do I get backpay after a successful appeal?
faqs.answer: SASSA has 14 business days to process backpay after receiving the tribunal ruling. Backpay includes all months from the original decline date.

faqs.question: Can I appeal if I do not know why I was declined?
faqs.answer: Yes. Select 'Other' as the reason on the appeal form and explain your situation. The tribunal will investigate.

faqs.question: What if I missed the 90-day deadline?
faqs.answer: Unfortunately, you cannot appeal after 90 days. You must submit a completely new grant application.

faqs.question: Can I appeal in person at a SASSA office?
faqs.answer: Yes, for non-SRD grants. Visit your nearest SASSA office with your documents and request a manual appeal submission.

faqs.question: Do I need to appeal every declined month for SRD?
faqs.answer: Yes. Each month is assessed independently. You must appeal each month that shows 'Declined'.
